title: Pre-norm and post-norm: where the normalisation sits
why: It shows the placement the prose describes in sequence, and what it changes: in pre-norm the residual path is untouched, so the Jacobian keeps its identity term I; in post-norm the normalisation sits on the path.
nodes: scalar product: (1 + b s)(1 + a s)
notes: Flow diagram, not axes. Left-to-right: residual stream x_l enters attention sublayer and MLP sublayer; each sublayer reads LN(x) in pre-norm and adds its output back to the stream. A parallel post-norm branch places LN after each residual addition. Label residual additions as the shared stream path. Below, show the Jacobian identity term I plus sublayer Jacobian factors, and the scalar derivative product with symbols s, a, b only, no invented values. The norm recurrence labels the three terms of the squared norm update. | Residual path: x_l plus f_l gives x_{l+1}; norm grows if f_l aligns with x_l or is orthogonal, can shrink if opposed; constant additive f_l=a gives x_N=x_0+N a. Normalization branch: LayerNorm computes per-token mean μ and variance σ over d features, then γ_i(x_i-μ)/σ+β_i; RMSNorm computes r=sqrt((1/d)Σx_i^2+ε) and outputs γ_i x_i/r, dropping mean subtraction. No axes; arrows flow from x_l/f_l to residual sum and from token vector x to either normalization pipeline. | Two parallel flows: pre-norm sends x through LN, then f, then adds the unnormalized residual x; post-norm adds x + f(x) first, then applies LN, so the residual path passes through J_LN. Label the post-norm derivative ∂y/∂x = J_LN(x + f(x))(I + J_f(x)); label the LayerNorm Jacobian entries with γ_i/σ, δ_ij, 1/d, and z_i z_j/d from the chapter. No axes; arrows show dataflow. Quantities are structural: d components, γ, σ, μ, z_i; no numeric values beyond those already in the prose. | Left-to-right residual path: embedding -> blocks -> final LN -> unembedding. Mark that no normalization occurs inside pre-norm blocks, so stream norm can drift; final LN controls only the unembedding input. Attention branch branches from x: W_Q/W_K -> reshape heads -> QK-norm over d_head -> dot product / sqrt(d_head) -> softmax. Label QK-norm site after projections and reshape, before dot product; gamma length d_head. Inset comparison from chapter: d_head=2, q=[10,0], k1=[10,0], k2=[0,10] gives scaled logits 100/sqrt(2)≈70.7 and 0, softmax ≈1 and ≈0, Jacobian max ≈6.14e-6; q=[1,0], k1=[1,0], k2=[0,1] gives scaled logits 0.707 and 0, softmax 0.669 and 0.331, Jacobian entries ≈0.197. Also note two-logit softmax example: logits 0 and 12 give probabilities ≈6.14e-6 and 0.99999386; logits 0 and 1 give 0.269 and 0.731. | Axes: horizontal = exponent range, vertical = mantissa precision. Plot bf16 and fp16 as two configurations; label exponent/fraction bit counts and fp16 max finite 65504. Mark the 640,000 dot-product value beyond fp16 range. A side annotation shows the pipeline q,k -> normalize -> dot product -> softmax, with overflow at the dot product and vanishing Jacobian at softmax saturation. All quantities come from the chapter.
